A mixing engineer, a video editor or a collaborator on another program usually wants the parts, not the mix. A stems export renders every track to its own file, all the same length and aligned to the project start, and packs them into one archive.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **File → Export Audio → Export multiple, split by tracks**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-second-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
4. Choose **File → Export audio**, set **Mode** to **Individual stems (archive)**, set **Format** to **WAV** and press **Start export**. When the render finishes, a download link for the `.zip` file appears in the dialog. Each track becomes a WAV inside the ZIP, trimmed to the same length so they line up when imported elsewhere.

## Tips

- Mute and solo do not affect stems; every track is rendered.
- Name the tracks before exporting — the stem files take their names from them.

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
